newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate dips to 4.9 percent in June.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate dips to 4.9 percent in June.

text.p: Florida's unemployment rate edged down to 4.9 percent in June from 5 percent in May, the state Department of Labor and Employment Security said Tuesday.
The data represent 348,000 unemployed Floridians out of a civilian labor force of 7.14 million.
Monroe County had the lowest unemployment rate for June, 2.1 percent, and Gulf and Hardy counties had the highest, 19.5 percent.
Of Florida's 67 counties, 34 had lower unemployment rates in June than a year ago. St. Lucie County had the largest over-the-year delcine, dropping three percentage points to 11.6 percent.
Total nonfarm employment grew by 223,800 jobs or 3.6 percent over the year to 6.4 million.
Services added the most jobs over the year, 109,900, and had the fastest growth rate, 5.2 percent. Trade saw the second biggest gain, adding 56,500 jobs over the year for a 3.5 percent growth rate.
Construction grew by 7,600 jobs or 2.3 percent over the year but remained well below the 1988-89 peak. Manufacturing grew by 3,300 jobs or 0.7 percent, with most of the increase in durable goods.
Transportation, communications and public utilities increased by 11,200 jobs or 3.6 percent. Finance, insurance and real estate grew by 13,600 jobs or 3.4 percent.
Government added 21,400 jobs over the year for a 2.3 percent growth rate, with all of the gains in state and local government.
